swim.governs: Steps and rock ledges straight into deep water on the tip of Sandycove Point, swum at every state of the tide. What changes your swim is the sea: an east or north-east wind blows straight in.
swim.deepBasis: Swum at all stages of the tide, subject to the sea state, with submerged rocks a hazard especially at low water (travelextra.ie wild swimming guide). Wikipedia gives about 6 m of water at high tide; spring tides here fall about 3.3 m (Marine Institute), which still leaves a few metres at low water. Nobody publishes a measured depth.
swim.tideNote: The tide doesn't decide whether you can swim here, but at low water the rocks under the steps come closer to the surface: look before you jump.
swim.lifeguard: No lifeguard at the Forty Foot (Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council); the beach next door at Sandycove has lifeguards in summer.

tide.basis: The Marine Institute's predictions for Bray Harbour, 8 km south (a model station), used as they are: no time or height shift. Its predictions for the Dublin Port gauge, 9.5 km the other side, agree on high water to within a minute on average and on low water to within 6 minutes (2026; single tides vary by up to about 10 minutes either way, because high water in Dublin Bay is long and flat).
